backwards_compatibility_rules.rule: Existing numeric P-lane strings remain readable and must not be rewritten by this plan.
Composite aliases may be added in future surfaces only as advisory metadata until separately promoted.
P103-P107 keep research-canary meaning in repo history; temporal operator P103-like routes remain NOT_COMPUTABLE without explicit evidence.
Status surfaces must preserve highest_lane=P102G and lane_count=58 during planning-only work.
Artifact consumers must accept legacy lane_id while new consumers may read composite_lane_id when present.

canonical_global_id_policy.rule: Canonical global continuity IDs remain the observed spine lane IDs until a separately authorized migration changes them.

explicit_non_execution_boundary.reason: Migration plan is advisory-only and cannot rename, move, rewrite, execute, authorize, or mint.

migration_phases.objective: Keep P102G as the highest observed lane and use the namespace audit as the read-only evidence base.
Adopt hybrid global IDs plus branch-local aliases in README, AGENTS, and PLANS doctrine without renaming files.
Plan status fields that can display canonical_global_lane_id and branch_local_alias side by side.
Prioritize P103-P107 research-canary versus temporal-continuity ambiguity before lower-risk collisions.
Run repeated deterministic validations before any future migration execution proposal.

artifact_naming_policy.rule: Do not rename existing artifact directories during planning.
Future composite-aware artifacts should expose namespace_id and branch_local_alias fields inside payloads before path changes are considered.

composite_identifier_format.rule: Format is <NAMESPACE_ID>.<P_LANE_ID> using uppercase namespace tokens and existing P-lane spelling.

doctrine_naming_policy.rule: README, AGENTS, and PLANS should describe canonical global IDs separately from branch-local aliases.
Documentation must not imply that branch-local aliases grant routing or execution authority.

runner_naming_policy.rule: Keep existing runner filenames stable; future namespace-aware runners may add payload metadata before any filename migration.

schema_naming_policy.rule: Keep existing schema filenames stable; future schemas may add optional composite_lane_id fields under explicit compatibility gates.

collision_remediation_order.reason: Critical research-canary versus temporal-continuity interpretation ambiguity.
Remaining namespace collisions after critical ambiguity is stabilized.

orphaned_reference_remediation_order.action: Classify each as documentation drift, missing source evidence, or intentionally blocked NOT_COMPUTABLE handoff.
Preserve terminal marker semantics unless future doctrine changes them.

risk_register.mitigation: Keep all alias fields advisory-only and require separate governance for any routing use.
risk_register.risk: Composite aliases could be mistaken for routing authority.

risk_register.mitigation: Preserve P102G, lane_count 58, FROZEN, ADVISORY_ONLY, and NOT_COMPUTABLE in planning artifacts.
risk_register.risk: Status pages could imply lane-count or highest-lane migration before evidence exists.

risk_register.mitigation: Require RESEARCH_CANARY.P103-P107 aliases and keep temporal operator P103-like route blocked.
risk_register.risk: P103-P107 could be interpreted as temporal operator authorization sequence instead of research-canary history.

risk_register.mitigation: Add composite IDs only as additive metadata in future work; do not remove legacy lane_id fields.
risk_register.risk: Downstream consumers may only understand legacy numeric lane_id fields.

stabilization_window.completion_condition: Three consecutive validation-only passes with unchanged P102G source state and no new downstream lane.

status_surface_transition_policy.rule: Future status surfaces may add composite namespace metadata only additively while preserving legacy highest_lane and lane_count fields.
